art.prompts: kept in the maintainer's working tree at taffy-core/ui/android/core/ui/vendor/start-scenes/prompts.md; not published

notes: Paths are relative to the repository root, not to this file.
WHY THIS TOOL RUNS NO ENCODER. Every other pack builder in this tree takes
an upstream corpus and produces the shipping bytes from it, so the encoder
is part of what it decides and is pinned and refused on mismatch. Here the
artwork is first-party and the reviewed 640 by 480 WebPs are committed:
they are the bytes a person looked at, and re-encoding them at package
time would ship bytes nobody reviewed. The `encoder` block above records
the recipe those files were made with so that a replacement is made the
same way; the provenance record is where it is enforced, by checksum.
WHY 640 BY 480. The plate is drawn at 168 dp at its widest, which is 672
pixels on xxxhdpi at 4x -- but it is decorative art behind a wordmark, not
a diagram, and the source decodes it with an `inSampleSize` chosen from
the width actually asked for, so the pixels that matter are the ones a
phone at 3x asks for and gets exactly. One size rather than a bucket per
density, for the reason the flag pack gives: a density-qualified pack is
several packs, each needing its own row, digest and publication decision.
WHY 4:3. The committed browsing plate this stands in for is 4:3, and
`TaffyStartSceneImage` draws both in one frame. A second ratio would mean
the page changing shape when the pack lands.
WHY THE PATH CARRIES NO PLUS SIGN, AND IS LOWER CASE. IsRelativePath in
taffy-core/browser/core_asset_validation.cc permits only a-z, 0-9, '.',
'-', '_' and the separator, which is a strict subset of what the catalog
generator accepts. A revision spelled with a '+' would generate cleanly
and be refused on the device.
WHY A NOTICE TRAVELS INSIDE THE ZIP. The pack reaches a device through the
delivery plane and is in no build graph, so nothing carries a notice onto
a generated credits page for it. The artwork is first-party and
proprietary, and the member inside the archive is the only statement of
that which arrives with the bytes it covers. The flag pack's LICENSE
member is the same rule for a third-party corpus.
